beginner.label: Beginner
beginner.blurb: Ten large, steady companies, equal weights, a tenth always in cash. Looks at the list twice a year and otherwise does nothing.
rules: Universe: companies worth over $100B, with volatility under 40% a year.
Picks the 10 with the best mix of calm (60%) and 12-month trend (40%), at most 2 per sector.
Reviewed in January and July only. No stops, no market timing.

intermediate.label: Intermediate
intermediate.blurb: Fifteen companies picked for trend and calm, equal weights. Reviews every three months and holds more cash when the whole market is in a downtrend.
rules: Skips anything with volatility over 45% a year. Picks the 15 best on 12-month trend (40%), 6-month trend (20%), calm (30%) and nearness to the 52-week high (10%), at most 4 per sector.
If the S&P 500 is below its 200-day average, only 75% invested.
Reviewed in January, April, July and October.

experienced.label: Experienced
experienced.blurb: Run like a hedge fund. Ranks every stock on trend and calm, holds up to 20 (no more than 4 per sector), sizes each by how bumpy it is to hit a risk target, reviews monthly, cuts any position that falls 18% from its high, and shrinks the whole book in a downtrend or when market volatility spikes.
rules: Only considers stocks above their own 200-day average with a positive 12-month trend and volatility under 70% a year.

Ranks them: 12-month trend 45%, 6-month trend 25%, calm 20%, nearness to the 52-week high 10%. Takes the top 20, at most 4 per sector, and keeps current holdings unless they slip well down the ranking.
Weights by 1 / volatility, no more than 8% each, then scales the whole book so its estimated volatility is about 20% a year (never more than 100% invested).
Halves the book if the S&P 500 is below its 200-day average; cuts it 25% more when the S&P's 3-month volatility is above 25%.
Sells any position that closes 18% below its highest close since it was bought, and waits for the next monthly review to reconsider it.
Reviewed on the first trading day of every month.
